newsitem.title: NORWAY: Explosions in Norway biker gang house, one dead.
newsitem.headline: Explosions in Norway biker gang house, one dead.

text.p: Three explosions demolished the clubhouse of a Norwegian motorcycle gang, killing a woman bystander and injuring four other people, police said on Thursday.

The explosions, which went off just before midnight (2200 GMT) on Wednesday, destroyed the headquarters of biker gang Bandidos in the town of Drammen south of Oslo, police spokeswoman Ann Lisbeth Hjelle said.
She declined to speculate if the incident was part of a turf war between rivalling biker gangs in the Nordic region.
Justice Minister Gerd-Liv Valla said police would now intensify surveillance of motorcycle gangs.
"I don't know in great detail what police are doing in this matter, but I know it has high priority," Valla told Norwegian radio. "It will get even higher priority."
Over the past three years at least eight people have been killed in Sweden, Denmark, Norway and Finland in fights between the rival Hells Angels and Bandidos gangs, both offshoots of U.S. bike clans.
Hjelle said police did not know what caused the explosions but news media speculated a car bomb had been set off.
She said the explosions killed a woman in her 50s who was driving past the building.
Eyewitnesses told the Norwegian news agency NTB that several people came running out of the house after the explosion, which smashed windows and walls and set off a fire.
Hjelle said four people had been taken to hospital suffering from shock and the effects of smoke inhalation.
Valla said she was studying the possibility of banning motorcycle gangs from having clubhouses in towns.
"We shall do all in our power to fight this kind of crime which now also is affecting completely innocent people," the justice minister said.
